ab-testing-prompts.title: Split traffic between two prompt variants
ab-testing-prompts.goal: Route incoming requests to two different prompts and log user ratings to find the better one.
steps: Set up a simple router script to randomly assign incoming user queries to Prompt A or Prompt B.
Call the LLM using both prompts and capture the generated outputs.
Collect a thumbs-up or thumbs-down feedback score from the user interface for each response.
Calculate the win rate for each prompt variant using a basic metrics aggregation script.
ab-testing-prompts.stretch: Add automated statistical significance testing to stop the test early when one prompt clearly wins.

agent-loop.title: Build a basic model reasoning and tool loop
agent-loop.goal: Write a Python script where an LLM calls a math tool, receives the output, and continues until finished.
steps: Define a simple Python function like a calculator or a current time checker.
Write a `while` loop that sends the user goal and available tool definitions to the LLM API.
Check if the model's response requests a tool call, and if so, execute the matching Python function.
Append the tool execution result back into the conversation history and loop again until the final answer is reached.
agent-loop.stretch: Add a maximum step counter to prevent infinite loops when the model gets stuck.

agent.title: Build a file search and summary agent
agent.goal: Create a script that lists local files, reads matching documents, and answers questions about them.
steps: Write three distinct Python tools: list directory, read file text, and search text.
Configure an LLM client with system instructions explaining when and how to use these tools.
Implement a execution loop to handle tool calls returned by the model.
Test the agent with a multi-step user request like finding a specific note and summarizing it.
agent.stretch: Give the agent a memory log file so it can recall findings across separate tool calls.

batching.title: Process text queries in asynchronous batches
batching.goal: Group multiple independent LLM prompts into a single script run to improve throughput.
steps: Create a JSON list of fifty distinct short text classification tasks.
Write an asynchronous Python script using `asyncio` to send requests in groups of ten.
Measure total execution time compared to sending requests sequentially one by one.
Handle API rate limit errors gracefully with automatic exponential backoff retries.
batching.stretch: Format the requests into an OpenAI Batch API file upload to secure a discount on token costs.

bm25.title: Implement a keyword search engine with BM25
bm25.goal: Build a local document search script using the BM25 ranking algorithm without vector embeddings.
steps: Install an open-source keyword ranking library like `rank_bm25`.
Load a folder of fifty text files and split them into individual words or tokens.
Index the tokenized documents using the BM25 algorithm.
Run keyword queries against the index and print the top three matching document snippets.
bm25.stretch: Combine BM25 keyword scores with vector similarity scores using reciprocal rank fusion.

caching.title: Cache LLM responses with a local SQLite database
caching.goal: Save model outputs to disk so identical queries return instantly without calling the paid API.
steps: Set up a local SQLite database table with columns for query hash, prompt text, and response.
Write a wrapper function that checks the database for an existing query hash before calling the LLM.
Store new model outputs in the database immediately after receiving them.
Test the wrapper by running the same query twice and verifying zero network calls on the second run.
caching.stretch: Add a Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration timestamp so cached entries automatically invalidate after 24 hours.

chain-of-thought.title: Compare standard and step-by-step prompts
chain-of-thought.goal: Test how forcing an LLM to explain its reasoning affects math or logic puzzle accuracy.
steps: Gather a test set of ten tricky word problems with known numerical answers.
Run all ten problems through an LLM using a direct answer prompt and record the scores.
Run the same problems using a chain-of-thought prompt like 'Think step by step before answering'.
Compare the accuracy percentage of both approaches in a summary table.
chain-of-thought.stretch: Extract the reasoning steps using regex and check if the model arrived at the correct answer for the right reasons.

chunking.title: Split long documents with overlapping chunks
chunking.goal: Write a Python function that divides a long text file into smaller overlapping segments for retrieval.
steps: Write a script that reads a multi-page article or book chapter from a text file.
Implement a sliding window function that splits the text into chunks of 500 characters.
Add a 50-character overlap between adjacent chunks to prevent cutting sentences in half.
Print the resulting chunks to verify their sizes and boundary points.
chunking.stretch: Implement semantic chunking by splitting text wherever embedding distance between sentences spikes.

content-moderation.title: Build a pre-flight content moderation filter
content-moderation.goal: Create a lightweight script that screens user inputs for toxic or unsafe language before sending them to an LLM.
steps: Write a Python function that calls a free moderation endpoint or uses a small local classifier model.
Define trigger categories such as hate speech, self-harm, or prompt injection attempts.
Wrap your main LLM application entry point with a check against this moderation function.
Return a polite refusal message to the user if the input trips the safety classifier.
content-moderation.stretch: Log flagged inputs to a local CSV file with timestamps for manual review later.

context-engineering.title: Assemble a dynamic context window builder
context-engineering.goal: Write a script that gathers system prompts, user history, and retrieved facts into an optimized prompt payload.
steps: Create modular text templates for system instructions, few-shot examples, and retrieved context.
Write a function that calculates total token counts using a tokenizer library like `tiktoken`.
Build a trimming routine that drops the oldest conversation messages if the total token count exceeds a limit.
Assemble the final ordered dictionary payload ready for the LLM API call.
context-engineering.stretch: Add priority weighting so critical system rules are never dropped when trimming context.

context-window.title: Visualize context window limits on a long text file
context-window.goal: Write a script that measures token count per section and flags text that overflows a target limit.
steps: Load a multi-page text file or document.
Use a tokenizer library like tiktoken to count tokens section by section.
Print a breakdown showing which paragraphs fit and which exceed the limit.
context-window.stretch: Add a sliding window chunker that splits the text into safe overlapping segments.

cost-tracking.title: Build a simple API wrapper that logs cost per call
cost-tracking.goal: Log prompt tokens, completion tokens, and estimated cost to a local database every time an LLM is called.
steps: Write a wrapper function around the OpenAI or Anthropic API client.
Extract usage metadata (prompt and completion token counts) from the API response.
Calculate cost using standard pricing rates and save the record to a SQLite table.
cost-tracking.stretch: Create a lightweight dashboard view using Streamlit to display spend by user ID.

distillation.title: Generate a synthetic dataset from a large model
distillation.goal: Use a powerful model to generate answers for your prompts, then format them for training a smaller model.
steps: Write a script to send 100 domain-specific prompts to a high-end model and save the outputs.
Format the prompt-response pairs into JSONL files suitable for fine-tuning.
Validate the file structure against a lightweight open-source training tool format.
distillation.stretch: Fine-tune a small local model using Hugging Face TRL on your generated dataset.

document-ingestion.title: Parse messy PDFs into clean chunks with metadata
document-ingestion.goal: Extract text from raw PDF files, strip unwanted headers and footers, and split them into structured chunks.
steps: Use a PDF parser library to extract raw text and page numbers from sample documents.
Write cleaning functions to remove repeated headers, footers, and page numbers.
Split the cleaned text into paragraphs with associated source metadata.
document-ingestion.stretch: Export the chunks into a structured JSON format ready for vector database insertion.

dpo.title: Format preference data for direct optimization
dpo.goal: Create and validate a JSONL preference dataset containing chosen and rejected model outputs.
steps: Gather a list of common user prompts in your domain.
Write a script to pair each prompt with one clearly better answer (chosen) and one flawed answer (rejected).
Validate the schema to ensure it matches standard DPO training requirements.
dpo.stretch: Write a script that tests dataset balance by checking average response lengths for both choices.

drift.title: Detect vocabulary shift in user inputs over time
drift.goal: Compare the keyword distribution of last week's user prompts against this week's prompts to spot drift.
steps: Collect two batches of text inputs representing different time periods.
Tokenize and count word frequencies in both batches, ignoring common stop words.
Calculate the difference in top terms to identify new vocabulary or topics.
drift.stretch: Compute embedding distance between the two batches to measure semantic drift numerically.

embeddings.title: Build a semantic search tool over personal notes
embeddings.goal: Generate vector embeddings for local text files and search them using cosine similarity.
steps: Read a folder of text notes and split them into short paragraphs.
Call an embedding API to convert each paragraph into a vector of floats.
Write a search function that computes cosine similarity between a query vector and your notes.
embeddings.stretch: Use a lightweight vector index like FAISS or ChromaDB instead of raw numpy arrays.

error-analysis.title: Tag and categorize LLM failures in a spreadsheet
error-analysis.goal: Build a systematic error categorization workflow to find out why an LLM prompt fails.
steps: Collect 50 prompt-response pairs where the system output was incorrect.
Define 4 common failure tags (e.g., hallucination, missing context, format error).
Manually tag each failure and generate a summary count of the most frequent issues.
error-analysis.stretch: Write a Python script that parses your tagged CSV and plots a failure frequency chart.

evals.title: Write unit tests for a prompt template
evals.goal: Create an automated test suite that checks LLM outputs against required keywords and length constraints.
steps: Write a list of test cases with inputs and expected assertions (e.g., contains keyword X).
Send the inputs to your prompt template via an API call.
Assert that the outputs pass the programmatic checks and print a test summary.
evals.stretch: Add an LLM-as-a-judge check to evaluate the semantic correctness of the output.

fallback-models.title: Implement an automatic retry and fallback proxy
fallback-models.goal: Write a client wrapper that catches API rate limits and errors, switching to a backup model automatically.
steps: Write a function that calls your primary model provider.
Wrap the call in a try-except block that catches timeout and rate-limit errors.
Route the request to a cheaper backup model if the primary call fails.
fallback-models.stretch: Add exponential backoff delays before triggering the fallback model.

few-shot-prompting.title: Build a Strict CSV Formatter with Input Examples
few-shot-prompting.goal: Force an LLM to parse messy text into structured CSV without extra conversational filler.
steps: Write three distinct examples of raw text mapped to the exact desired CSV output format.
Append a new unseen messy text sample to the prompt without any examples.
Call an LLM API and verify that the output matches the exact CSV header and delimiter pattern.
Refine the examples to fix any column alignment edge cases.
few-shot-prompting.stretch: Add an invalid input example to show the model how to output an empty state instead of guessing.

fine-tuning.title: Fine-Tune a Tiny Model on Custom JSON Data
fine-tuning.goal: Train a small open-weights model to consistently output jokes in a specific pirate dialect.
steps: Gather 50 clean prompt-completion pairs in the required chat JSONL training format.
Upload the dataset and run a budget fine-tuning job using an open platform like Together AI.
Download or host the resulting model weights and write a local test script.
Compare the base model output against your fine-tuned model output on the same prompt.
fine-tuning.stretch: Split your dataset into a training set and a test set to measure accuracy improvements.

function-schema.title: Define Tools for a Weather and Calculator Assistant
function-schema.goal: Write explicit JSON function schemas so an LLM can pick and call the right tool.
steps: Write valid JSON schemas for a weather lookup function and a basic calculator function.
Pass the schemas into an LLM client call that supports native tool calling.
Send a user query like 'What is 45 times 12?' and extract the structured tool call argument.
Execute the local function logic and return the result back to the model for a final response.
function-schema.stretch: Add strict parameter constraints and descriptions to handle missing user arguments gracefully.

golden-dataset.title: Curate a Golden Dataset for a Support Bot
golden-dataset.goal: Build a versioned CSV reference file of tricky customer questions and verified ideal answers.
steps: Collect 20 historical customer support tickets along with their verified correct resolutions.
Format the inputs and expected outputs into a clean, version-controlled JSON or CSV file.
Write a quick evaluation script that checks new model answers against this reference file.
Calculate a baseline correctness score using exact match or semantic similarity.
golden-dataset.stretch: Automate the evaluation script to run in GitHub Actions every time the reference file changes.

gpu-serving.title: Serve an Open Model Locally with vLLM
gpu-serving.goal: Spin up a local high-throughput inference server for a 7B parameter open-weights model.
steps: Set up a Python virtual environment and install vLLM alongside PyTorch.
Download a compact open model like Llama-3-8B-Instruct from Hugging Face.
Launch the vLLM server with PagedAttention enabled on your local GPU.
Send an OpenAI-compatible API request from a local Python script to test generation speed.
gpu-serving.stretch: Benchmark the tokens-per-second throughput under concurrent requests using Apache Bench.

grounding.title: Build a Source-Cited Answer Generator
grounding.goal: Force an LLM to output inline citations pointing back to supplied reference text paragraphs.
steps: Provide three reference paragraphs about a niche historical event in the prompt.
Instruct the model to answer a question using *only* the text and append bracketed source IDs.
Write a regex validator that checks if every citation in the response matches a provided source ID.
Test the validator with a question that requires information not present in the sources.
grounding.stretch: Automatically reject answers that reference source IDs that do not exist in the context.

guardrails.title: Build an Input and Output Safety Filter
guardrails.goal: Intercept malicious user prompts and toxic model outputs before they reach the user.
steps: Write a lightweight keyword and regex check to flag prompt injections and common attacks.
Implement a secondary classifier call using a small model to check for toxic language.
Wrap your main LLM application logic inside a pipeline that runs these checks before and after.
Return a polite refusal message whenever a guardrail trips.
guardrails.stretch: Log all blocked prompts and responses to a local SQLite database for auditing.

hallucination.title: Detect Unsupported Claims in Generated Summaries
hallucination.goal: Write a script that catches when an LLM invents facts not found in the source text.
steps: Generate a summary of a factual article using a high-temperature LLM setting to force errors.
Write a prompt for a separate verification model asking it to break the summary into individual claims.
Check each individual claim against the original source text to see if it is supported.
Output a hallucination score based on the percentage of unsupported claims.
hallucination.stretch: Automatically highlight unsupported sentences in red using a simple command-line interface.

human-in-the-loop.title: Create an Approval Workflow for AI Drafts
human-in-the-loop.goal: Pause an automated email generator so a human can edit and approve drafts before sending.
steps: Write a script that generates a customer outreach email draft using an LLM.
Save the generated draft to a local JSON file with a status of 'pending_approval'.
Build a simple command-line prompt that lets a user edit the text or approve it.
Update the status to 'approved' and simulate dispatching the final version.
human-in-the-loop.stretch: Build a minimalist local web UI using Streamlit to make reviewing and editing drafts easier.

hybrid-search.title: Combine BM25 and Vector Search in Python
hybrid-search.goal: Merge keyword search results with vector embeddings to improve document retrieval accuracy.
steps: Load a small text corpus into a local SQLite database for keyword lookups using BM25.
Generate vector embeddings for the same corpus using a free local embedding model.
Write a query function that runs both searches and normalizes their scores.
Combine the score lists using reciprocal rank fusion to produce a final ranked list.
hybrid-search.stretch: Compare retrieval precision between pure vector search and hybrid search on a set of test queries.

indirect-prompt-injection.title: Build an RSS summary reader that catches malicious prompt payloads
indirect-prompt-injection.goal: Process untrusted web content containing hidden prompt instructions and stop them from executing.
steps: Write a python script to fetch RSS feeds from test blogs containing injected text strings.
Pass the fetched text directly into an LLM summarization pipeline without sanitization.
Implement a secondary guardrail parser to flag structural anomalies in the returned output.
Refactor the pipeline to isolate external data inside strict system delimiters.
indirect-prompt-injection.stretch: Add a classification step that scans inbound feeds for hidden instructional phrases before sending them to the main model.

inference.title: Build a local token counter and cost tracker for model inference
inference.goal: Track precise latency and per-token compute costs while executing a local open-weight model.
steps: Download a small open-weight model using Ollama or Hugging Face Transformers.
Write a wrapper script to measure time-to-first-token and total generation time.
Calculate cost metrics dynamically based on standard API pricing tiers.
Log request parameters, tokens generated, and execution time to a local CSV file.
inference.stretch: Build a simple web dashboard using Streamlit to visualize inference latency across different prompt lengths.

jailbreak.title: Build an automated prompt mutation script to test safety limits
jailbreak.goal: Systematically test an LLM's safety boundaries by applying text transformations to restricted prompts.
steps: Define a list of benign baseline queries that trigger standard safety refusals.
Write a python function to apply base64 encoding, leetspeak, and roleplay wrappers to the queries.
Send the mutated prompts to an LLM endpoint and record the response codes and text.
Analyze which specific transformations successfully bypass the safety filter.
jailbreak.stretch: Build a scoring script that automatically classifies model responses as compliant, refused, or partially compliant.

kv-cache.title: Measure generation speedup gained by using a KV cache
kv-cache.goal: Demonstrate how storing attention states accelerates token generation in autoregressive models.
steps: Write a basic next-token prediction loop in PyTorch from scratch for a tiny transformer.
Run generation without caching and measure the compute time for each additional token.
Implement a basic key-value cache array that stores previous attention states.
Compare the total execution time of the cached loop against the un-cached loop.
kv-cache.stretch: Calculate the exact RAM usage difference between cached and non-cached states as sequence length scales up.

latency.title: Build a latency percentile monitor for LLM API calls
latency.goal: Measure and log p50, p90, and p99 response times for an LLM endpoint under load.
steps: Write a script that fires concurrent requests to an LLM endpoint using asyncio.
Capture the start and end timestamp for every individual request.
Calculate p50, p90, and p95 latency percentiles from the collected metrics.
Plot the latency distribution over time using a lightweight charting library.
latency.stretch: Simulate network jitter and track how intermittent timeouts impact the p99 latency metric.

llm-as-judge.title: Build an automated evaluation pipeline using LLM-as-Judge
llm-as-judge.goal: Grade a set of model-generated text outputs against a reference rubric using an independent LLM.
steps: Gather a dataset of fifty prompt-response pairs that require qualitative evaluation.
Write a structured prompt template containing a clear grading rubric and output schema.
Send each pair and the rubric to a capable model like GPT-4o-mini or Claude 3 Haiku.
Parse the JSON responses from the judge model into a summary spreadsheet of scores.
llm-as-judge.stretch: Test for positional bias by swapping the order of candidate answers and running the judge evaluation a second time.

llm-gateway.title: Build a lightweight proxy gateway for API key management
llm-gateway.goal: Route model requests through a custom local proxy that handles logging and fallback providers.
steps: Write a basic FastAPI server that accepts standard chat completion payloads.
Implement a routing layer that forwards requests to either OpenAI or Anthropic based on config.
Add request and response logging to a local SQLite database with timestamps.
Handle API rate limit errors by automatically retrying with an alternative provider.
llm-gateway.stretch: Add a simple token bucket rate limiter to protect your downstream application from exceeding budget limits.

llm.title: Build a tiny character-level language model from scratch
llm.goal: Train a minimal neural network in PyTorch that predicts the next character in a text file.
steps: Load a small text file like Shakespeare's works and convert characters to integer indices.
Define a simple embedding and linear layer stack using PyTorch.
Write a training loop with cross-entropy loss to optimize next-character prediction.
Generate new text by sampling characters autoregressively from the trained model.
llm.stretch: Upgrade the model architecture from a simple feedforward network to a tiny single-head attention block.

lora.title: Fine-tune a small model on custom text using a LoRA adapter
lora.goal: Train a low-rank adaptation matrix on a custom dataset without modifying the base model weights.
steps: Prepare a JSONL dataset containing fifty examples of a specific writing style.
Load an open-weight base model and apply PEFT LoRA configuration settings.
Run the training script using Hugging Face TRL or Unsloth on a free cloud GPU.
Save the resulting adapter weights separately from the base model.
lora.stretch: Compare the generation output of the base model against the LoRA-adapted model using identical prompts.

mcp.title: Build a custom Model Context Protocol server for local files
mcp.goal: Create a local server that exposes directory search tools to an MCP-compatible client.
steps: Initialize a node or python project using the official Model Context Protocol SDK.
Define a tool schema that accepts a directory path and search query string.
Write the file-scanning execution logic to safely read local text files.
Connect your new server to an MCP-enabled desktop client and test tool discovery.
mcp.stretch: Add a second tool to the server that allows the LLM to write and save notes directly to disk.

memory.title: Build a SQLite conversation memory layer
memory.goal: Store and retrieve past chat turns to give your assistant persistent context across sessions.
steps: Set up a local SQLite database with tables for threads and messages.
Write a function that appends user and assistant turns after each call.
Inject the last N relevant messages into the system prompt context.
Test recall by starting a new session and asking about earlier details.
memory.stretch: Add a background summarization step that compresses old messages into a running profile when history grows too long.

metadata-filtering.title: Build a filtered vector search tool
metadata-filtering.goal: Combine hard attribute constraints with semantic similarity to narrow down retrieval results.
steps: Create a small document collection tagged with categories and dates.
Index documents and metadata into a local vector store like Chroma.
Write a query function that applies a metadata filter before similarity search.
Verify that restricted queries exclude records outside the filter criteria.
metadata-filtering.stretch: Build a parser that extracts filter tags directly from user prompts using a small regex or LLM classifier.

model-routing.title: Build a cost-aware model router
model-routing.goal: Automatically direct queries to a cheap model for simple tasks and a strong model for complex ones.
steps: Define criteria for simple versus complex queries using length or keyword heuristics.
Write a routing function that sends requests to local Ollama or cheap API endpoints based on the check.
Fallback to a heavier model if the first response indicates failure.
Log routing decisions and cost savings for a batch of mixed queries.
model-routing.stretch: Train a tiny classifier model to handle routing decisions instead of relying on hardcoded heuristics.

multi-agent.title: Build a writer and editor agent pair
multi-agent.goal: Coordinate two distinct LLM roles where one drafts content and the other reviews and refines it.
steps: Define system prompts and task boundaries for a writer agent and an editor agent.
Write a Python script that passes the writer's draft to the editor.
Allow the editor to send revision requests back to the writer in a loop.
Print the final output and the message history between agents.
multi-agent.stretch: Add a third critic agent that scores the draft and terminates the loop when the score clears a threshold.

multimodal.title: Build an automatic chart data extractor
multimodal.goal: Send chart images to a vision model and output structured CSV data from the visual elements.
steps: Gather a few sample charts or graphs as image files.
Write code to send these images to an open-weight vision model or API.
Prompt the model to extract data points into a clean JSON format.
Save the returned JSON as a downloadable CSV file.
multimodal.stretch: Build a simple web interface where users can drag and drop images and download the resulting CSV.

observability.title: Build an LLM call logger and tracer
observability.goal: Capture prompt tokens, latency, costs, and outputs for every LLM interaction in a local dashboard.
steps: Write a wrapper function around your LLM calls to measure execution time and token usage.
Store each trace record in a local SQLite database with a unique run ID.
Build a minimal web view using Streamlit to display recent traces and costs.
Trigger errors deliberately to confirm exception traces are recorded correctly.
observability.stretch: Add nested span tracing so you can inspect individual steps inside multi-step workflows.

online-vs-offline-evals.title: Build an offline test runner and online logger
online-vs-offline-evals.goal: Compare evaluation results from a static test dataset against feedback logged from live runs.
steps: Create a JSON file with 10 test prompts and expected output keywords.
Write an offline script that scores model responses against this test set.
Add a live logging hook that saves production inputs and user thumbs-up or down signals.
Compare the offline accuracy score against the ratio of positive online feedback.
online-vs-offline-evals.stretch: Automate the offline test runner to execute every time you update your prompt templates.

open-weight-models.title: Run and prompt a local open-weight model
open-weight-models.goal: Download, run, and query an open-weight language model entirely on your local hardware.
steps: Install Ollama or Llama.cpp on your local machine.
Download a lightweight open-weight model like Llama 3 or Mistral.
Write a short Python script using the local endpoint to generate text.
Measure the tokens per second generated on your machine.
open-weight-models.stretch: Modify the model's system prompt or generation parameters via a local configuration file.

orchestrator-worker.title: Build a research report generator
orchestrator-worker.goal: Use an orchestrator to break a topic into subtopics, fetch content in parallel workers, and merge results.
steps: Write an orchestrator prompt that splits a broad research topic into three subquestions.
Run concurrent worker calls to generate text answers for each subquestion.
Pass all worker outputs to a final aggregation prompt to synthesize a coherent report.
Test the flow with different research topics and verify coherence.
orchestrator-worker.stretch: Let the orchestrator dynamically decide how many workers to spawn based on topic complexity.

pairwise-evals.title: Build a side-by-side model comparison tool
pairwise-evals.goal: Compare two model outputs for the same prompt and record a preference vote to rank them.
steps: Write a script that sends a single prompt to two different model configurations.
Build a simple command-line or web interface that displays both anonymous answers.
Prompt the user or an LLM judge to pick the better response and state why.
Save the win-loss records to a CSV file to determine the preferred variant.
pairwise-evals.stretch: Implement the Bradley-Terry statistical model to calculate dynamic Elo ratings for each model configuration.

pii-redaction.title: Build a Local PII Scrubber
pii-redaction.goal: Filter names, emails, and phone numbers out of text before sending it to an external API.
steps: Set up a Python script using regex or spaCy for named entity recognition.
Write a function to mask detected entities with placeholder tokens like [EMAIL].
Test the scrubber on a dummy dataset containing sensitive sentences.
Integrate the redaction step into an existing API logging pipeline.
pii-redaction.stretch: Handle edge cases like obfuscated email addresses and international phone numbers without ruining the rest of the text.

planning.title: Build a Task Decomposition Agent
planning.goal: Make an agent write a step-by-step execution plan before attempting a multi-part goal.
steps: Write a system prompt forcing the model to output a numbered JSON list of steps.
Build a loop that executes the first step and passes the output to the next.
Add a re-planning step if a task execution fails or returns an error.
Test the agent on a complex multi-file text summarization task.
planning.stretch: Allow the agent to dynamically insert or remove steps from its plan as it learns new information.

prompt-caching.title: Benchmark Prompt Caching Costs
prompt-caching.goal: Measure how prompt caching reduces latency and token costs for a large system prompt.
steps: Send a large context document (e.g., a software codebase) to an LLM provider multiple times.
Configure the API request headers or parameters to enable prompt caching.
Measure and log the time-to-first-token and cost difference between cached and uncached calls.
Write a brief summary report of your findings.
prompt-caching.stretch: Calculate the cache expiration TTL break-even point for your specific request frequency.

prompt-injection.title: Build a Prompt Injection Sandbox
prompt-injection.goal: Demonstrate how untrusted user input can hijack an LLM application and test a defense.
steps: Build a simple customer support bot that reads untrusted user review data.
Craft a malicious review input that instructs the bot to reveal its system instructions.
Implement a delimiter separation or two-model defense to isolate untrusted data.
Verify that the malicious input is treated as raw data rather than instructions.
prompt-injection.stretch: Implement a secondary classification model that screens incoming text for injection patterns before processing.

prompt-versioning.title: Build a Git-Backed Prompt Registry
prompt-versioning.goal: Store prompts in a version-controlled directory and load them via unique IDs in code.
steps: Create a repository folder structure to store prompts as individual markdown or JSON files.
Write a small Python loader utility that reads a prompt file by its version tag.
Log the loaded prompt version ID alongside model outputs in your application database.
Make a change to a prompt, commit it, and verify the app uses the new version.
prompt-versioning.stretch: Add a metadata header to each prompt file tracking author, description, and performance evaluation scores.

prompt.title: Construct a Structured Prompt Template
prompt.goal: Combine system instructions, few-shot examples, and user input into a reliable prompt format.
steps: Define clear XML-style tags for instructions, context, and examples.
Write a Python function using f-strings to inject dynamic user variables into the template.
Test the template across five different edge-case inputs to check adherence.
Refine the prompt layout to minimize token usage while maintaining accuracy.
prompt.stretch: Write an automated unit test suite that validates the prompt outputs required JSON keys consistently.

quantization.title: Run a Quantized Local Model
quantization.goal: Compare the RAM usage and generation speed of a 4-bit model versus a 16-bit model.
steps: Download a small open-source model in GGUF format using a tool like Ollama or llama.cpp.
Monitor your system RAM and GPU VRAM usage while running an inference pass.
Download a heavier unquantized version of the same model size.
Compare output quality and hardware resource consumption between the two formats.
quantization.stretch: Plot a latency-versus-perplexity curve for 2-bit, 4-bit, 8-bit, and 16-bit versions of the same base model.

query-rewriting.title: Build a Query Rewriting Pipeline
query-rewriting.goal: Transform ambiguous user questions into clear, explicit search queries before RAG retrieval.
steps: Write a prompt that takes chat history and a vague follow-up question as input.
Have a fast model output a standalone search query containing all necessary context.
Pass the rewritten query into a vector search database lookup.
Compare retrieval relevance scores between raw user queries and rewritten queries.
query-rewriting.stretch: Generate three diverse variations of the user query in parallel to improve multi-angle retrieval coverage.

rag.title: Build a Local Mini-RAG System
rag.goal: Answer questions over a local text file using vector embeddings and an LLM.
steps: Chunk a local text document into smaller paragraphs using Python.
Generate embeddings for each chunk using a free local embedding model or lightweight API.
Store embeddings in an in-memory vector index like FAISS or Chroma.
Retrieve top matching chunks for a user question and format them into an LLM prompt.
rag.stretch: Implement a sliding-window chunking strategy with overlap and measure its effect on answer accuracy.

rate-limits.title: Build a Rate-Limited API Client
rate-limits.goal: Implement token bucket throttling and exponential backoff to handle provider rate limits safely.
steps: Write a Python wrapper around an LLM API call that catches rate-limit exceptions (HTTP 429).
Implement exponential backoff with jitter to retry failed requests automatically.
Add a token bucket queue to throttle outgoing requests per minute.
Test your client by sending a burst of concurrent requests against a mock server.
rate-limits.stretch: Add automatic fallback to a secondary cheaper model provider when the primary provider hits a rate limit.

react-pattern.title: Build a ReAct loop with a calculator tool
react-pattern.goal: Code a minimal ReAct agent that loops between reasoning steps and calculator tool calls until it solves a math query.
steps: Set up a local Python script using a base LLM and a simple add/multiply Python function as a tool.
Write a prompt template that forces the model to output a Thought, an Action, and wait for an Observation.
Parse the model's text output to extract tool names and arguments, then execute the function.
Feed the tool result back into the conversation history and run the loop until the final answer appears.
react-pattern.stretch: Add a web search API tool and let the agent handle multi-step questions that require both math and external facts.

reasoning-models.title: Compare standard and reasoning model outputs on puzzles
reasoning-models.goal: Write a script that benchmarks a reasoning model against a standard model on tricky logic puzzles and checks output quality.
steps: Select a set of five difficult logic or math word problems that standard models often fail.
Write code to query both a standard chat model and a reasoning model via their respective APIs.
Log the time taken, token count, and correctness for each model response.
Print a summary comparing latency and accuracy differences between the two architectures.
reasoning-models.stretch: Inspect the hidden or visible chain-of-thought tokens to see where the reasoning model catches its own mistakes.

red-teaming.title: Build an automated prompt injection red teamer
red-teaming.goal: Create a script that bombards a custom assistant prompt with adversarial inputs to find safety bypasses.
steps: List ten common jailbreak and prompt injection patterns (e.g., ignore previous instructions, roleplay overrides).
Write a test harness that feeds these adversarial strings into your target LLM application.
Use a secondary judge LLM to evaluate whether the target model successfully resisted the attack.
Output a simple vulnerability report showing which injection styles successfully leaked system instructions.
red-teaming.stretch: Incorporate a self-mutating attack loop where the script uses failure outputs to generate smarter follow-up attacks.

regression-evals.title: Set up automated regression evals for prompt updates
regression-evals.goal: Build a CI-style eval script that prevents prompt updates from breaking previously passing test cases.
steps: Create a JSON file containing ten input queries and their corresponding golden reference answers.
Write a Python script that runs the current prompt against all ten test cases.
Use an LLM-as-a-judge score function to check if the new output matches or exceeds the required quality threshold.
Exit with a non-zero error code if any test case score drops below the historical baseline.
regression-evals.stretch: Hook the script into a GitHub Action so it automatically runs and comments on pull requests that modify prompt files.

reranking.title: Add a cross-encoder reranker to keyword search
reranking.goal: Improve basic text search results by passing the top candidates through a dedicated cross-encoder reranker model.
steps: Retrieve the top twenty text chunks for a query using simple keyword or vector search.
Load a lightweight open-source cross-encoder reranker model from Hugging Face.
Score each candidate document pair-wise against the query using the reranker.
Sort the documents by the new scores and output only the top five highest-ranking results.
reranking.stretch: Measure latency trade-offs by timing how long the reranker takes compared to the initial retrieval step.

retries-and-timeouts.title: Build a resilient API wrapper with retries and timeouts
retries-and-timeouts.goal: Write a Python client wrapper that safely handles rate limits, network timeouts, and transient server errors.
steps: Write a wrapper function around an LLM API call that enforces a hard timeout limit.
Implement exponential backoff logic to catch rate limit errors and wait before trying again.
Add a maximum retry count to stop infinite loops when the API is completely down.
Test your wrapper by mocking network failures and verifying it recovers cleanly.
retries-and-timeouts.stretch: Add a fallback mechanism that switches to a secondary backup model provider if the primary provider fails all retries.

retrieval-metrics.title: Calculate MRR and Recall@K for a mini RAG pipeline
retrieval-metrics.goal: Write a evaluation script that computes retrieval performance metrics against a labeled ground-truth dataset.
steps: Create a test set of five queries, each paired with the exact ID of the correct document that should be retrieved.
Run your retrieval system to return the top 5 document IDs for each test query.
Write functions to calculate Recall@5 and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) across your test queries.
Print the final metric scores to the console.
retrieval-metrics.stretch: Plot a graph showing how Recall changes as you increase K from 1 to 10.

rlhf.title: Fine-tune a model using direct preference optimization
rlhf.goal: Take a base model and use a preference dataset to align its outputs using DPO (Direct Preference Optimization).
steps: Download a small public preference dataset containing prompt, chosen, and rejected response pairs.
Set up a training script using a library like TRL or Hugging Face Trainer configured for DPO.
Run a short training job on a low-cost cloud GPU instance using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA).
Compare the outputs of the base model versus your aligned model on sample prompts.
rlhf.stretch: Format your own custom preference dataset from logged chat thumbs-up and thumbs-down clicks.

semantic-caching.title: Build a semantic cache to save API costs
semantic-caching.goal: Create a caching layer that returns previous LLM answers when a new prompt is semantically similar to an old one.
steps: Set up a local vector store or SQLite database to hold queries, embeddings, and responses.
When a new user query arrives, generate its embedding vector.
Search your cache for an existing query with a cosine similarity score above 0.92.
Return the cached response if a match is found; otherwise, call the LLM and save the new pair.
semantic-caching.stretch: Track and log the estimated dollar amount saved by the cache across fifty repeated or rephrased test queries.

similarity-search.title: Build a local semantic search engine from scratch
similarity-search.goal: Index a folder of text files and search them by meaning using local embeddings and cosine similarity.
steps: Write a script to read text files from a local folder and split them into paragraph chunks.
Generate vector embeddings for each chunk using a free local embedding model.
Store the vectors and text chunks in a simple numpy array or a local vector database.
Take a text query, embed it, compute cosine similarity against all chunks, and print the top matches.
similarity-search.stretch: Add a command-line interface so you can query your document folder interactively in your terminal.

speculative-decoding.title: Build a mini speculative decoding script
speculative-decoding.goal: Write a script that uses a small draft model to guess tokens and a large model to verify them in one pass.
steps: Load a tiny language model and a base language model using Hugging Face transformers.
Write a loop where the small model generates a short draft of upcoming tokens.
Pass the draft sequence through the large model in a single forward pass to check acceptance.
Compare output speeds against standard autoregressive generation.
speculative-decoding.stretch: Implement a threshold check to dynamically adjust draft length based on how often the draft model guesses correctly.

speech-to-text.title: Build a local voice memo transcriber
speech-to-text.goal: Create a command-line tool that turns local audio files into written transcripts using Whisper.
steps: Install OpenAI-Whisper and ffmpeg on your local machine.
Write a Python script that accepts an audio file path as an argument.
Process the audio with a local Whisper model to generate text with timestamps.
Save the resulting transcript to a clean markdown file.
speech-to-text.stretch: Add speaker diarization using pyannote.audio to separate different voices in a meeting recording.

streaming.title: Build a real-time streaming text client
streaming.goal: Build a web app that displays model responses token by token as they arrive over the network.
steps: Set up a basic FastAPI backend that calls an LLM API with streaming enabled.
Create a minimal HTML and JavaScript frontend that reads the server-sent events stream.
Update the DOM incrementally as each text chunk arrives from the server.
Measure and display the total generation time once the stream completes.
streaming.stretch: Add a typing indicator that fades out once the first token arrives and a smooth auto-scroll effect.

structured-output.title: Build an invoice data extractor
structured-output.goal: Extract vendor names, dates, and line items from messy invoices into a strict JSON schema.
steps: Define a Pydantic model representing the expected schema for the invoice data.
Configure an LLM client to enforce structured output using the Pydantic schema.
Write a script that sends sample invoice text to the model.
Validate that the returned JSON matches the required schema without parsing errors.
structured-output.stretch: Handle schema validation failures gracefully by feeding the error back to the model for self-correction.

supervised-fine-tuning.title: Fine-tune a model on custom instructions
supervised-fine-tuning.goal: Train an open-weights model on a small dataset of custom prompt-response pairs using QLoRA.
steps: Format a small CSV dataset of input prompts and target responses into JSONL.
Set up an Unsloth or Hugging Face training script with 4-bit quantization.
Run the fine-tuning loop for a few epochs on a cloud GPU notebook.
Test the trained model against the base model on held-out prompts.
supervised-fine-tuning.stretch: Evaluate the fine-tuned model against the base model using an automated LLM-as-a-judge scoring script.

system-prompt.title: Build a persona-constrained support bot
system-prompt.goal: Write a system prompt that forces an LLM to follow strict rules, tone, and formatting constraints.
steps: Draft a multi-section system prompt detailing persona, forbidden topics, and output structure.
Write a test suite of ten edge-case user inputs designed to break the rules.
Iterate on the prompt wording to patch loopholes discovered during testing.
Bundle the system prompt into a simple chat script.
system-prompt.stretch: Add automated assertions in your test script to check if model responses violate any system rules.

temperature.title: Build a temperature comparison visualizer
temperature.goal: Generate the same creative sentence at various temperature settings to visualize output variance.
steps: Write a Python script that calls an LLM API multiple times with a creative prompt.
Iterate temperature values from 0.0 to 1.5 in fixed increments.
Collect responses for each temperature setting and print them side by side.
Observe how low values repeat deterministic text while high values introduce novel phrasing.
temperature.stretch: Calculate and plot the token overlap or embedding distance between outputs across different temperatures.

text-to-speech.title: Build a text-to-speech reading assistant
text-to-speech.goal: Convert a local text file into an audio podcast using an open-source text-to-speech engine.
steps: Install a Python library like Kokoro or edge-tts.
Write a script that reads a text file and splits it into manageable sentence chunks.
Loop through the chunks to synthesize speech audio files.
Concatenate the audio chunks into a single playable MP3 file.
text-to-speech.stretch: Add multi-voice support by assigning different speakers to alternating paragraphs in the text.

throughput.title: Build a load testing script for LLM APIs
throughput.goal: Measure tokens per second and requests per second under concurrent load against a local endpoint.
steps: Write an asynchronous Python script using asyncio and httpx to send concurrent requests.
Simulate multiple users sending prompts to a local vLLM or Ollama instance.
Track total generation time, output token counts, and error rates.
Calculate aggregate throughput metrics across all concurrent workers.
throughput.stretch: Plot a latency-versus-throughput curve by gradually increasing the concurrency level until errors occur.

time-to-first-token.title: Build a latency tracker for LLM requests
time-to-first-token.goal: Measure and log the time elapsed between sending a prompt and receiving the first generated token.
steps: Write a script that records a high-resolution timestamp right before sending an API request.
Listen to the streaming response chunk stream using an async client.
Record a second timestamp upon receiving the very first text chunk.
Compute the difference and print the Time to First Token (TTFT) in milliseconds.
time-to-first-token.stretch: Compare TTFT across different input prompt lengths to see how prompt size affects prefill duration.

tokenizer.title: Build a custom byte-pair encoding tokenizer
tokenizer.goal: Write a Python script from scratch that trains a simple BPE tokenizer on a small text file and encodes new text.
steps: Count character pair frequencies in a sample text corpus.
Merge the most frequent pair into a new vocabulary token.
Repeat the merge process until reaching a target vocabulary size.
Write encode and decode functions to convert strings to integer ID arrays.
tokenizer.stretch: Add regex pre-tokenization rules to prevent the tokenizer from merging across punctuation marks, matching real-world behavior.

tokens.title: Build a token-budget cost calculator
tokens.goal: Create a command-line tool that estimates API costs and tracks character-to-token ratios across different model tokenizers.
steps: Install official tokenizers libraries for popular open and proprietary models.
Write a function to count tokens for any input text file.
Calculate estimated input and output costs based on current pricing tiers.
Output a summary table comparing token counts across different models.
tokens.stretch: Build a local web UI using Streamlit that highlights individual tokens with alternating background colors as you type.

tool-calling.title: Build a CLI assistant with a calculator tool
tool-calling.goal: Create a Python script where an LLM decides when to call a local math function to answer user questions.
steps: Define a Python function for safe arithmetic evaluation.
Configure the LLM client schema with the function definition.
Send a user prompt, parse the model's tool call JSON response, and run your function.
Send the function result back to the model to generate the final answer.
tool-calling.stretch: Add a second tool that fetches current weather from a free public API and let the model choose between tools.

top-p-sampling.title: Build a custom token sampler script
top-p-sampling.goal: Write a raw Python script that takes a list of next-token probabilities and applies top-p filtering.
steps: Create a dictionary of dummy tokens and their floating-point probabilities.
Sort the tokens in descending order of probability.
Calculate cumulative probabilities and slice off tokens once they exceed threshold p.
Renormalize the remaining probabilities and sample a token using random choices.
top-p-sampling.stretch: Combine both temperature scaling and top-p filtering into a single sampling function with adjustable parameters.

tracing.title: Build a lightweight request tracer
tracing.goal: Write a Python wrapper that logs timing, inputs, and outputs of nested function calls to a local SQLite database.
steps: Create a SQLite table to store span names, start times, durations, and payloads.
Write a context manager or decorator that measures elapsed time for any block of code.
Wrap a multi-step LLM workflow with your decorator to capture inner steps.
Query the database to print a formatted execution tree of a run.
tracing.stretch: Render the recorded execution traces as an interactive collapsible tree view in a local HTML page.

transformer.title: Build a tiny self-attention module
transformer.goal: Implement scaled dot-product attention from scratch using NumPy to understand how tokens interact.
steps: Create random query, key, and value matrices for a small sequence of token vectors.
Compute the dot product of queries and keys to get raw attention scores.
Scale the scores by the square root of the head dimension and apply softmax.
Multiply the attention weights by the value matrix to produce context-aware vectors.
transformer.stretch: Extend the single-head attention function into multi-head attention by splitting the hidden dimension.

turn-detection.title: Build an audio silence turn detector
turn-detection.goal: Write a Python script that monitors a microphone stream and flags when a user stops speaking.
steps: Capture live audio chunks in Python using a basic audio library.
Calculate the Root Mean Square amplitude for each incoming audio buffer.
Track consecutive silent chunks against a threshold time limit.
Trigger a callback function once the silence duration confirms a completed turn.
turn-detection.stretch: Integrate a lightweight Voice Activity Detection library to distinguish human speech from background noise.

user-feedback-loops.title: Build an LLM output thumbs rating app
user-feedback-loops.goal: Create a minimal web app that logs user thumbs-up and thumbs-down feedback alongside prompt inputs.
steps: Build a simple web interface with an input box and output display.
Add thumbs-up and thumbs-down buttons next to each generated response.
Save the prompt, response, rating, and timestamp to a local JSON file.
Write a summary script that prints out prompts that received negative ratings.
user-feedback-loops.stretch: Add a text input field for optional user comments when a negative rating is submitted.

vector-database.title: Build a pure Python vector search engine
vector-database.goal: Write a lightweight script that stores float vectors and performs cosine similarity search without external DB software.
steps: Generate or load a set of sample text embeddings.
Write a cosine similarity function using basic vector math.
Implement a search function that compares a query vector against all stored vectors.
Return the top K closest vectors along with their similarity scores.
vector-database.stretch: Add metadata filtering so you can restrict searches to items matching a specific category tag.

voice-agents.title: Build a text-to-speech voice loop
voice-agents.goal: Create a local script that takes typed input, sends it to an LLM, and speaks the response aloud.
steps: Set up an API client for text generation.
Integrate an offline text-to-speech library like pyttsx3 or system speech tools.
Write a loop that reads user input from the terminal, gets the LLM reply, and speaks it.
Handle basic conversational history so the agent remembers prior statements.
voice-agents.stretch: Add speech-to-text input so you can talk to the agent through your microphone instead of typing.

workflows-vs-agents.title: Compare a scripted pipeline to a loop-based agent
workflows-vs-agents.goal: Build a fixed multi-step text summarizer, then refactor it into an agent that decides when to stop.
steps: Write a Python script that chains two prompts together in a fixed sequence for summarization.
Add a conditional router step to the script based on the model's first output.
Convert the structure into a dynamic loop where the LLM decides its own next tool call.
Compare the predictability, token cost, and failure modes of both approaches.
workflows-vs-agents.stretch: Log the exact prompt tokens and execution time for both designs across fifty test inputs to find the cost-reliability tradeoff.
